title: Native Crash 与 tombstone：从 signal 到 backtrace
key_conclusions: Native crash analysis should start from signal or abort reason, then combine fault address, registers, backtrace, memory map, allocator evidence, symbols, and reproduction context.
Backtrace is the current execution path, not always the root memory-corruption site; UAF and overflow often require sanitizer or malloc_debug evidence.
Fault address interpretation requires maps and registers because null, heap, guard, code, stack, mmap, and unmapped addresses imply different next steps.
Reliable acceptance requires replaying the crash scenario with no tombstone, no allocator or sanitizer report, and stable related memory evidence.
shallow_points: The article does not include a real tombstone decoded line by line.
It does not validate tombstone formats, debuggerd fields, or signal details across Android versions, ABIs, and vendor ROMs.
It does not include a runnable crashing native sample for null dereference, UAF, double free, overflow, SIGBUS, and stack overflow.
It does not show a real symbolication workflow with unstripped symbols and source-line mapping.
